A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OGMM research, with readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–E. All research content can be matched; v2's extra page results from bibliography reflow.

before.justification: v1 reports original graph-classification experiments and ablations in Tables 1–2, plus homogeneous-backbone and large-scale graph/node-classification results in Appendix C, Tables 4–5.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results in Tables 1–2 and Appendix C, including graph/node-classification comparisons, ablations, and sensitivity analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same label-conditional graph generator, classifier masks, sparse MoE gating, regularizers, and two-stage optimization procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate MUTAG, PTC, REDDIT-B, and NCI1, plus ogbg-Molhiv, ogbn-Arxiv, and Twitch in Appendix C.4. Graph/node-classification tasks and edge-density, temporal, and regional shift scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 1, 4, and 5 retain Avg-PTM, Ens-Prob, Ens-HighConf, Uni-Soup, Greedy-Soup, Inverse-X, and Multi-GFKD in their corresponding comparisons. Table 1 also retains the same individual GCN, GAT, and GIN baselines.

E3.justification: The domain partitions, accuracy/precision metrics, two-layer GNNs with 32 feature dimensions, and 200/20-epoch generation/merging budgets remain unchanged. Appendix C retains the same supplementary evaluation protocols.

E4.justification: Section 4.2 and Appendix C retain the same component ablations, mask-placement and gradient analyses, homogeneous-backbone tests, hyperparameter and sample/domain-count sensitivity studies, and graph visualizations.

E5.justification: Appendix B.2 states in both versions that results report means and standard deviations over ten runs. The uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical results, rankings, plotted trends, and qualitative findings match throughout. For example, both report OGMM accuracy of 66.84 ± 0.45 on NCI1 in Table 1 and 53.38 ± 0.01 on ogbn-Arxiv in Table 5.

T1.justification: Assumption 3.1, Definition 3.2, Theorem 3.3, the Appendix A proofs and derivations, and the Appendix B.4 complexity analysis are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about data-free merging of heterogeneous graph models, the graph-generation and masked-MoE framework, and improved out-of-distribution generalization.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning classifier masks, synthetic graphs, and expert/domain diversity are unchanged. Appendix E retains the same limitations involving the mixture-distribution assumption, unseen classes, pretrained-model quality, and scaling.

D1.justification: Both disclose the same optimizer, hyperparameter grids, epoch counts, algorithm pseudocode, RTX 4090D hardware, and code-access link. No implementation or reproducibility information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The same 69 references and research-positioning discussions remain, including Appendix D. Reference [69] moves to a separate page in v2 but is not a new citation.

P1.justification: The arXiv margin stamp changes from v1 dated 4 June 2025 to v2 dated 17 March 2026. The scientific prose, author list, terminology, headings, and section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Increased bibliography spacing on page 13 pushes reference [69] onto an otherwise nearly empty page 14, shifting the appendices by one page. Tables 1–5 and Figures 1–17 retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, empirical evidence, proofs, reproducibility information, and limitations are unchanged. The updated arXiv stamp and bibliography reflow, including the nearly empty extra page, produce no meaningful net change in overall paper quality.
